title: 660-28 engine no-crank: battery, starter feed, ground and interlocks

steps.instruction: Move the unit to an approved service position, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels. With the required operator controls in their normal start positions, command START once and observe the starter without holding the key. Confirm whether this is a no-crank complaint rather than an engine that cranks but does not start.
steps.question: Does the starter remain stationary and fail to rotate the engine when START is commanded?

steps.instruction: Before meter work, verify the normal starting state against the operator manual: transmission selector actually in neutral, parking brake applied, seat/operator-presence conditions met, emergency stop reset where applicable, and no active start-inhibit indication. Do not jumper any interlock.
steps.question: Are all required operator and interlock conditions genuinely satisfied, with control positions and indications agreeing?

steps.instruction: Switch off and inspect the starting-battery case, hold-down, posts, clamps, main power lead, engine ground strap and accessible starter connections. Look for looseness, corrosion, broken strands, heat damage and evidence of previous jump-start polarity damage. Do not make repairs until the required electrical isolation is complete.
steps.question: Are the battery and accessible power/ground connections physically serviceable and secure?

steps.instruction: Measure and record open-circuit voltage directly across the starting-battery posts using a DVOM. Compare only with the battery/equipment manufacturer's resting-voltage criterion for the actual battery type and condition; nominal system voltage is not an acceptance range. If an approved criterion is not available, stop and obtain it rather than guessing pass/fail.
steps.question: Does the recorded resting voltage meet the applicable manual criterion?

steps.instruction: Keep the DVOM across the battery posts. Have an assistant make a normal START command while all required interlocks remain functional, and record the minimum stable cranking voltage. Do not extend cranking to obtain a number. Compare with the manual's cranking-voltage and duration requirements.
steps.question: Does battery voltage during cranking remain within the applicable manual acceptance range?

steps.instruction: Measure voltage drop from the battery positive lead post to the starter main B+ stud during cranking. Use the complete feed first; if excessive, repeat segment by segment to locate the cable, lug, connection or contact causing the drop. Keep leads clear of hot and rotating parts.
steps.question: Is the positive-feed voltage drop within the maximum allowed by the applicable manual?

steps.instruction: Move the meter to measure ground-side voltage drop from the starter housing/designated starter ground to the battery negative lead post during cranking. Test the whole return path first and then the engine-to-chassis and chassis-to-battery segments if needed.
steps.question: Is the ground-side voltage drop within the maximum allowed by the applicable manual?

steps.instruction: With the main feed and ground demonstrated good, back-probe the starter solenoid S/control terminal to battery negative during a normal START command. Note both measured voltage and whether the solenoid clicks. Do not short the adjacent B+ terminal and do not bypass the control circuit.
steps.question: Is the solenoid control-terminal voltage within the applicable manual range while START is commanded?

steps.instruction: Isolate the machine before any mechanical inspection or component removal.
steps.terminal_result: Main feed, ground and solenoid control are good but the original no-crank remains. Suspect the starter solenoid/motor or mechanical engine drag/lock. First verify by the manufacturer method that the engine is free to rotate with ignition/fuel safely disabled and electrical energy isolated, then bench-test or replace the starter only if that test and inspection support it. Retest cranking after repair.

steps.instruction: Trace the start-control circuit using the applicable wiring diagram. With the selector verified in neutral and START commanded, back-probe the neutral-start switch output to battery negative without jumpering the switch. Inspect the connector and mechanical selector alignment while taking the reading.
steps.question: Is neutral-start switch output voltage present within the applicable manual range?

steps.instruction: Leave the safety interlocks functional and isolate the circuit before connector repair.
steps.terminal_result: Neutral-start output is present but the starter S terminal did not receive an acceptable control signal. Isolate the downstream open or high resistance between this switch and the solenoid: inspect the identified connectors, start relay or other series devices shown on the actual schematic, and repair wiring/connections or replace only a component proven faulty. Restore all interlocks and retest start/inhibit operation.

steps.instruction: Return the selector and controls to their normal positions and isolate before adjustment.
steps.terminal_result: Neutral-start output is absent or low. Verify real transmission neutral, selector linkage alignment and supply to the switch, then test the neutral-start switch and upstream start-command path against the wiring diagram. Adjust or replace only the item proven faulty; never defeat the neutral safety function. Confirm start occurs only in permitted selector positions after repair.

steps.instruction: Record the actual cranking and starting behavior before choosing another diagnostic path.
steps.terminal_result: This is not a no-crank fault. If the engine rotates but fails to start, leave this tree and diagnose cranking speed, fuel and ignition/combustion using the Ford engine and equipment procedures; check for a fuel leak before further cranking. A crank-no-start decision tree has not yet been seeded in this package.

steps.instruction: Do not continue to starter replacement until the normal start state can be achieved.
steps.terminal_result: Correct the operator setup and confirm whether cranking is restored. If physical control positions and their indications disagree, inspect the related seat/presence, parking-brake, neutral or emergency-stop switch, connector and linkage using the applicable schematic and adjustment procedure. Do not bypass an interlock; verify both permitted starting and prohibited starting states after repair.

steps.instruction: Isolate the battery before cleaning, tightening or replacing any high-current connection.
steps.terminal_result: Repair the identified visual/connection defect first: clean and protect serviceable battery connections, replace damaged leads to the specified routing and terminal practice, secure the battery, or replace a battery with case/terminal damage after confirming specifications. Repeat the complete connection inspection and resting/cranking voltage tests rather than installing a starter as the first repair.

steps.instruction: Identify the battery type before selecting a charger or charging profile.
steps.terminal_result: Resting voltage does not support a valid starter test. Charge the correct battery type by the approved method, then repeat resting voltage and an approved battery load/capacity test. If the battery passes, investigate charging performance and parasitic draw; if it fails, replace it with the specified type and recheck the starting circuit. Do not interpret a discharged battery alone as proof of an internally defective battery.

steps.instruction: Stop repeated start attempts while the low-voltage cause is unresolved.
steps.terminal_result: Battery voltage falls below the manual criterion under cranking load. Recharge and perform the approved battery load/capacity test, clean and secure connections, and check for abnormal starter current or mechanical drag if the battery is good. Do not condemn the starter until battery condition and cable loss have been separated from excessive starter/engine load.

steps.instruction: Isolate before disturbing the positive high-current feed.
steps.terminal_result: Excessive starter positive-feed voltage drop localizes unwanted resistance in the positive cable path. Compare segment drops to isolate the battery post/clamp, cable, lug, connector or series solenoid/contact, then clean, repair or replace only the defective section with correctly rated parts. Repeat the loaded voltage-drop test and confirm the repaired lead does not overheat.

steps.instruction: Isolate before removing ground straps or cleaning mating surfaces.
steps.terminal_result: Excessive ground-side voltage drop localizes resistance in the starter/engine/chassis/battery-negative return. Use segment tests to find the defective housing bond, engine strap, chassis connection, negative cable or clamp; repair the connection to clean, secure metal and replace damaged cable. Retest ground drop under load before evaluating the starter.

title: 600i Power Stow no lift or slow lift: supply, pressure, relief, cylinder and flow

steps.instruction: Remove baggage and other load. Move to an approved service area, park on level ground, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels. Inspect the loading head, conveyor, lift arms, hoses and cylinders for impact damage, obstruction, obvious external leakage or a person/tool in the travel path. Lower and mechanically support raised equipment before close inspection.
steps.question: Is the machine clear, unloaded and mechanically safe for a controlled hydraulic function test?

steps.instruction: With the lift in the manual-required checking position and pressure isolated, inspect reservoir level, fluid identity and condition, filler/breather and visible inlet hose. Look for aeration, milky contamination, debris and a collapsed or leaking suction line. Use only fluid allowed by the correct manual if correction is needed.
steps.question: Are oil level and condition correct and the visible pump inlet path free of obvious restriction or air entry?

steps.instruction: Test each Power Stow 12 V battery individually with a DVOM, then repeat using the manual-approved hydraulic load condition. Identify and preserve correct series connections. Record every reading rather than judging only total bank voltage; compare with the actual battery and equipment criteria before continuing.
steps.question: Does each auxiliary battery meet the applicable resting and loaded voltage criteria during the lift-pump supply test?

steps.instruction: Only after verifying the manufacturer test-port ID and full procedure, connect a rated gauge at the Power Stow main lift-pump outlet with energy isolated. Re-energize for the documented normal lift command and record pressure, oil temperature and pump-drive behavior. Do not hold at relief or deadhead a circuit unless explicitly instructed by the manual. Stop and escalate if the exact procedure/range is unavailable.
steps.question: Is the measured main lift pressure within the manual range for the prescribed lift test?

steps.instruction: With normal supply pressure demonstrated, use the manufacturer-provided cap-end pressure connection and supported loading-head procedure to determine whether pressure reaches the lift cylinder. Do not loosen a cylinder hose to improvise a test point. Keep personnel and leads outside the loading-head travel path.
steps.question: Does cap-end cylinder pressure meet the manual range and show that commanded pressure reaches the cylinder?

steps.instruction: Maintain the specified mechanical support and use the manufacturer-approved rod-end/return connection. Perform only the prescribed lift or hold test and record rod-end pressure/back-pressure to assess return restriction, check/counterbalance operation and possible cylinder internal leakage.
steps.question: Is rod-end/back-pressure within the manual range for the prescribed lift or hold test?

steps.instruction: Because main pressure was low, test the main relief valve only by the manufacturer relief-setting and isolation procedure. Check for contamination, premature opening, incorrect setting and unrestricted bypass. Do not turn an adjustment blindly and do not mask low pressure with a higher relief setting.
steps.question: Does the relief valve hold and open at the correct manual setting without evidence of premature bypass?

steps.instruction: With relief operation verified, have a qualified technician install the rated inline flow/pressure test set and measure pump delivery at the manufacturer-defined load, oil temperature and pump-drive condition. Record pressure and flow together; do not close the test-set load valve without a documented limit.
steps.question: Is pump delivery flow within the manual range under the prescribed load and operating conditions?

steps.instruction: Isolate and support before inspecting the cylinder feed path.
steps.terminal_result: Main pump pressure is available but does not reach the cylinder cap end correctly. Use the hydraulic schematic to isolate the loading-head control solenoid/spool, electrical command, obstructed line/hose and pilot-operated check valve. Verify command power and mechanical spool movement before replacing the cylinder; repair the proven restriction or control fault and repeat the supported functional test.

steps.instruction: Keep the loading head mechanically supported throughout mechanical inspection.
steps.terminal_result: Available cylinder pressures do not explain the no/slow movement, so inspect for mechanical binding, bent lift arms or cylinder rod, damaged pivots/slides, foreign-object obstruction and incorrect auto-level geometry. Unload the mechanism before checking free movement by the manufacturer method. If the mechanism moves freely and all readings genuinely meet specification, repeat the functional test with an approved loaded procedure rather than replacing parts.

steps.instruction: Isolate and support before separating any return or cylinder component.
steps.terminal_result: Abnormal rod-end/back-pressure indicates a return/check/counterbalance restriction or cylinder internal-bypass problem. Isolate these possibilities with the manufacturer pressure/hold test: inspect the return path and correct valve operation first, then evaluate cylinder seal leakage only after external causes are excluded. Correct any contamination source before returning the repaired circuit to service.

steps.instruction: Depressurize and isolate before removing or adjusting a relief valve.
steps.terminal_result: The relief valve is opening prematurely, bypassing, contaminated or incorrectly set. Follow the manufacturer clean/inspect/replace and adjustment procedure; find the cause of contamination or overheating rather than repeatedly resetting the valve. Adjust only to the cited specification with a calibrated gauge, lock the setting as directed and verify normal lift without increasing pressure beyond the manual limit.

steps.instruction: Recheck the test configuration before selecting replacement parts.
steps.terminal_result: Measured delivery is acceptable although the earlier main-pressure result was low. This is not proof of a defective pump: verify the flow/pressure test points and conditions, then isolate an unintended bypass through the relief/control circuit or an incorrect test configuration using the schematic. Repeat the pressure-versus-flow check and continue to the cylinder/valve branch only when readings are repeatable.

steps.instruction: Isolate electrical and hydraulic energy before pump or inlet service.
steps.terminal_result: Low pump delivery is confirmed. Check pump drive-motor voltage under load, connector drop, contactor/relay operation and actual motor speed first; then inspect reservoir supply, inlet hose and suction restriction for air entry or collapse. Replace the pump only after drive and inlet causes are excluded or pump testing proves wear/damage. Correct oil contamination and verify pressure and flow after repair.

steps.instruction: Tag the unit out of service until the observed hazard is corrected.
steps.terminal_result: Do not run a hydraulic function test with a person or tool in the travel path, aircraft conflict, damaged lift structure, obstructed mechanism or active external leak. Clear the area, secure and support the equipment, and repair structural/hose/cylinder damage under the manufacturer procedure. Restart this tree only after the unsafe condition is eliminated.

steps.instruction: Resolve fluid loss or contamination before further loaded testing.
steps.terminal_result: Correct low/incorrect/contaminated fluid or the visible inlet defect with the exact approved fluid and service procedure. Locate and repair the source of oil loss, aeration or water/debris entry; replace a restricted or collapsing inlet hose as indicated. Simply topping off is not a permanent repair. Check for pump damage after severe cavitation, then repeat this tree from the safe inspection.

steps.instruction: Identify the correct battery type and series configuration before charging or replacement.
steps.terminal_result: Auxiliary battery supply does not support the hydraulic pump load. Charge and test each battery by the approved method, inspect high-current cables and grounds for voltage drop, and verify charger operation. Replace weak batteries only to specification and in the matched manner required by the Power Stow maintenance manual. Repeat the loaded supply test before condemning the pump, relief valve or cylinder.

title: 660-28 PCS transmission will not shift out of Neutral: codes, power, signals, shift inhibit, pressure

steps.instruction: Check the transmission ID nameplate and the TCM label (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.1). This tree is for a PCS 4LHD/4LHDX transmission with a PCS TCM. Many GSE units only use F-N-R; Park is not used in GSE applications (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).
steps.question: Is this a PCS 4LHD/4LHDX transmission with a PCS TCM?

steps.instruction: Engine at idle, operator on the seat, service brake fully pressed, throttle released. Move the lever from Neutral to Forward, back to Neutral, then to Reverse. Do not rev the engine: the TCM blocks shifts out of Neutral while throttle is above 15% (PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Application Guide v2.0, §2.5.7.1, p.65).
steps.question: Does the transmission stay in Neutral (no drive) in both Forward and Reverse?

steps.instruction: Read transmission codes with the PCS TCM Diagnostic software, a J1939 code reader, or CAN Capture > Bus Monitor (DM1 from the transmission). A check-transmission light, if fitted, flashes stored codes with key on and engine off (PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Technician's Guide v2.0, Section 4, p.48).
steps.question: Are any transmission DTCs active or stored?

steps.instruction: Key on, engine off. Connect to the TCM with the PCS TCM Diagnostic software and the COM cable (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3). Without TCM power a Gen 3 valve body gives no forward and no reverse (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).
steps.question: Does the software connect to the TCM?

steps.instruction: Key on. Measure the TCM switched-ignition feed (pin 19) and battery feed (pin 20) to ground (pin 42 or 9). Check both 10 A fuses first.
steps.question: Is battery voltage present on both TCM feeds?

steps.instruction: In the software, move the shift lever through every range and watch the reported lever position (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3, Check the Signals 1).
steps.question: Does the reported lever position match the actual lever in every range?

steps.instruction: Watch the reported throttle position: it must read 0% with the pedal released and 100% at full pedal (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3). The TCM will not shift out of Neutral above 15% throttle (PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Application Guide v2.0, p.65); abuse protection is typically set at 15% (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).
steps.question: Does throttle read 0% released and 100% at full pedal?

steps.instruction: Start the engine. Compare engine RPM in the software with the actual engine speed. Abuse protection is typically set at 1500 RPM (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3). Most GSE units get RPM from the engine ECM over J1939 CAN (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2).
steps.question: Does reported RPM match actual RPM, at idle well below the abuse-protection limit?

steps.instruction: Open the Abuse Protection monitor screen. With the service brake fully pressed, check the shift-inhibit input (called 'Neutral Input' in the PCS software). On units with a brake pressure switch, this input tells the TCM the brakes are applied, which enables the shift from Neutral to Forward or Reverse (PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Application Guide v2.0, §2.5.7.2, p.65). Check any other abuse-protection inputs (seat switch etc.); these are vehicle specific (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).
steps.question: With the brake pressed, does the shift-inhibit input show active and are all other abuse-protection inputs satisfied?

steps.instruction: Check fluid level and condition with the engine at idle after moving the lever through the ranges to fill the cavities. The correct level depends on temperature (cold 80-90 °F / 26-32 °C, hot 180-200 °F / 82-93 °C); the software calculates it. Fluid should be red: dark and burnt-smelling suggests internal failure, cloudy or milky suggests water or coolant (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).
steps.question: Is the fluid at the correct level for its temperature, red, and not burnt or milky?

steps.instruction: Read the transmission part number on the ID nameplate to tell a 4LHD from a 4LHDX; the line pressure limits differ (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2).
steps.question: Is the transmission a 4LHD (not a 4LHDX)?

steps.instruction: Measure line pressure at the tap with 0 A commanded, in Neutral at 1200 RPM, fluid 100-200 °F.
steps.question: Is line pressure within the 4LHD range?
steps.spec_source: PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2, Line Pressure Tap table, 4LHD at 0 A

steps.instruction: Measure line pressure at the tap with 0 A commanded, in Neutral at 1200 RPM, fluid 100-200 °F.
steps.question: Is line pressure within the 4LHDX range?
steps.spec_source: PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2, Line Pressure Tap table, 4LHDX at 0 A

steps.instruction: Forward clutch solenoid test with the PCS TDD (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.4): all switches off, connect to the transmission (arrow out) and the battery, power LED on. With FWD and SSA/SSB ON, move the lever to Drive: the vehicle should move forward in 1st. Return to Neutral, turn FWD OFF, move to Drive: the vehicle should not move. Gen 3 valve bodies move regardless of lever position.
steps.question: Does the vehicle move forward with FWD ON and stay still with FWD OFF?

steps.instruction: Stop: this tree does not apply.
steps.terminal_result: Not a PCS 4LHD/4LHDX with PCS TCM. Use the manual for the fitted transmission and controller; do not apply PCS pin-outs, codes or pressures to it.

steps.instruction: Record what the transmission does instead.
steps.terminal_result: The transmission engages, so this is not a no-engagement complaint. If it slips, stays in one gear or shifts harshly, read the TCM codes first: many PCS codes put the transmission in 2nd gear, maximum line pressure or neutral as a failsafe (PCS codes in the DTC library, PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Technician's Guide v2.0, Section 4).

steps.instruction: Look up every code before going further.
steps.terminal_result: Diagnose the stored/active codes first. Look each one up in the DTC library (PCS codes, cited to PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Technician's Guide v2.0, Section 4, pp.48-52): codes 91-95 lock the transmission or command neutral, and others limit gears. Repair the cause, clear the code, and repeat this tree if it still won't engage.

steps.instruction: Check the COM cable and connector before replacing anything.
steps.terminal_result: TCM has power but will not communicate. Check the COM cable (A-TCM4182) and the communication connector. If it still won't connect with power present, the guide's next step is to try a different TCM (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.3).

steps.instruction: Isolate the battery before repairing wiring.
steps.terminal_result: Missing TCM feed. Repair the open fuse, connector or wire on the switched-ignition (pin 19) or battery (pin 20) feed, or the ground (pin 42/9). Find why a fuse blew before replacing it. Retest engagement.

steps.instruction: Isolate before adjusting the linkage.
steps.terminal_result: Lever position mismatch. Check that the shift cable fits the transmission detent and the shift arm is centred in each detent (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, pp.2-3), and check the lever position switch/manifold wiring. A wrong combination sets PCS code 28. Adjust or repair, then repeat the lever check.

steps.instruction: Isolate before working on the sensor.
steps.terminal_result: Throttle signal is wrong. With throttle reported above 15% the TCM will not shift out of Neutral. Check the TPS adjustment, sensor and its 5 V / signal / ground wiring (or the CAN throttle source); codes 21/22 cover circuit faults. Repair and recheck 0% / 100%.

steps.instruction: Check the RPM source.
steps.terminal_result: Engine RPM signal is wrong or missing. On J1939 units check the CAN link between engine ECM and TCM: twisted pair, two 120-ohm terminators, 60 ohms measured between CAN H (bulkhead pin 7) and CAN L (pin 1) with power off (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2). Use CAN Capture > Bus Monitor to confirm EEC1 from the engine. Repair and recheck.

steps.instruction: Isolate before working on the brake switch circuit.
steps.terminal_result: Shift-inhibit (brake) input not seen by the TCM, so it holds Neutral. Check the brake pressure switch and its wiring to the TCM shift-inhibit input. On the PCS example bulkhead this is pin 5, grey/white, Digital Input 5 (PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Application Guide v2.0, Figure 2.5.8-1, p.64), but harnesses vary: confirm the pin on the vehicle's own harness drawing (TODO: needs spec from manual for the TUG harness). Do not jumper or bypass this input: it is an abuse-protection safety input.

steps.instruction: Let the transmission cool before draining or filling.
steps.terminal_result: Fluid problem. Low fluid gives no or intermittent pressure; overfill can overflow when hot. Correct the level with the specified fluid (DEXRON VI, PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.1). Burnt or milky fluid indicates internal damage or contamination: find the source (vent, cooler/radiator, storage container) before refilling, and contact PCS.

steps.instruction: Stop the engine before removing the gauge.
steps.terminal_result: Line pressure out of range with signals and fluid good. Check the pressure control (line) solenoid circuit (PCS code 73) and the filter, then the pump and valve body per the PCS 4LHD/4LHDX Technician's Guide v2.0. Contact PCS (GSEhelp) with the readings before replacing the transmission.

steps.instruction: Save a datalog for PCS.
steps.terminal_result: The transmission engages under direct control, so the hydraulics and forward clutch work. The fault is in what the TCM sees or its calibration. Recheck the abuse-protection inputs while moving the lever, record a datalog (PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.2, How to Datalog), and contact PCS with it.

steps.instruction: Isolate before electrical tests.
steps.terminal_result: No engagement under direct control. Check the forward clutch solenoid circuit (PCS code 94) and the valve body generation (identify Gen 2 or Gen 3 by the pan/filter view or the solenoid resistance from Trans pin E to pins R and S, using the table in PCS 4-Speed Transmission Quick Reference Guide v1.3, p.1). If the circuit is good, the fault is internal: contact PCS before removing the transmission.

title: 660-28 PCS disc parking brake does not hold: inspect, burnish, adjust

steps.instruction: Park on level ground away from aircraft, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels. Hold-test method and acceptance: TODO: needs spec from manual. Confirm the complaint with the operator.
steps.question: Does the parking brake fail to hold the vehicle?

steps.instruction: Isolate the vehicle. Inspect the PCS 4LHD disc parking brake (MICO M515 caliper, PCS kit BRK2050): disc and pads for oil or grease (check the extension housing seal), damage or defects, and the apply arm, clevises and cable for binding or wrong adjustment. Do not install parts that show defects (PCS BRK2050 drawing, note 3).
steps.question: Are the disc, pads and linkage clean, undamaged and free to move?

steps.instruction: Check the service history.
steps.question: Were the pads, disc or brake newly installed and not yet burnished?

steps.instruction: MICO recommends burnishing right after installation and adjustment; maximum torque is reached only after burnishing (MICO Form 81-950-016 (Rev. 1998-10-14), Burnishing Procedures for MICO Caliper Disc Brakes, p.2). Parking-brake guideline (SAE J360 §7.3): 10 stops from 10 MPH at 3 ft/s² (0.9 m/s²), stops at least 2.5 miles (4000 m) apart, driving at 20 MPH between stops. These are guidelines only: use a clear route away from aircraft and people, obey airside speed limits, and contact the vehicle manufacturer if the unit cannot do this safely.
steps.question: Was the burnish completed as described?

steps.instruction: After burnishing, adjust the parking brake and its actuation to MICO specifications (MICO Form 81-950-016 (Rev. 1998-10-14), Burnishing Procedures for MICO Caliper Disc Brakes, p.2; adjustment values: TODO: needs spec from manual). After any dynamic stop made with the parking brake, inspect the brake and disc for unusual wear before returning to service. Repeat the hold check.
steps.question: Does the parking brake now hold?

steps.instruction: Record the conditions.
steps.terminal_result: Brake holds in this test. Record the slope, load and conditions the operator reported and recheck under those; final acceptance needs customer testing (MICO Form 81-950-016 (Rev. 1998-10-14), Burnishing Procedures for MICO Caliper Disc Brakes, p.2).

steps.instruction: Keep isolation in place for the repair.
steps.terminal_result: Repair what was found: replace contaminated or damaged pads/disc (fix the oil leak first), free or replace binding linkage, and correct the adjustment. New pads or disc then need burnishing: restart this tree.

steps.instruction: Escalate with the findings.
steps.terminal_result: A burnished, clean brake that still won't hold needs the adjustment and caliper checked against the MICO caliper disc brake manual (81-515-009) and the PCS kit documentation (adjustment values TODO: needs spec from manual). Contact TUG/PCS if it is in spec and still weak.

steps.instruction: Do not return to service on an unburnished brake without approval.
steps.terminal_result: Burnish not possible as written. Get an approved burnish procedure from the vehicle manufacturer (MICO Form 81-950-016 (Rev. 1998-10-14), Burnishing Procedures for MICO Caliper Disc Brakes, p.2 allows other procedures with similar braking conditions) before release.

steps.instruction: Record the work.
steps.terminal_result: Parking brake holds after burnish and adjustment. Record burnish completion, adjustment and the hold test on the work order.

steps.instruction: Escalate.
steps.terminal_result: Still weak after burnish and adjustment. Recheck for contamination and the actuation linkage, then contact TUG/PCS with the findings. Do not release the unit with a parking brake that does not hold.

title: 660-28 Ford MSG-425 2.5 L engine MIL on: read and look up the fault codes

steps.instruction: Start the engine and observe the engine MIL. Note the fuel in use (gasoline or LPG): some J1939 SPN/FMI pairs map to different DTCs by fuel type (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2).
steps.question: Is the engine MIL on with the engine running?

steps.instruction: Choose how to read codes. Faults can be read three ways: the GCP Display software, flashing out on the MIL, or a J1939 CAN display (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2). GSE Tech Pro's CAN Capture > Bus Monitor shows DM1 SPN/FMI from the engine (SA 00).
steps.question: Is a J1939 reader (or CAN Capture) available on this unit?

steps.instruction: Read the engine SPN/FMI pairs. Translate each to a DTC number with Section 3, CAN (J1939) to DTC Cross Reference (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', pp.16-22), using the fuel type.
steps.question: Did you read and translate at least one SPN/FMI?

steps.instruction: Key on, engine off. With the OEM MIL fitted (pin 6 of the 42-pin connector), ground pin 3 of the 42-pin connector to start the flash-out. The MSG425 first flashes 1-6-5-4 three times, then each fault code three times; 1-6-5-4 alone means no fault codes (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2). Confirm the 42-pin connector pins on the MSG425 schematic before connecting the ground lead.
steps.question: Did any fault codes flash after 1-6-5-4?

steps.instruction: Read the EDI calibration number on the GCP display (for example 3125D12F). Look at the digit just before the last letter (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.3).
steps.question: Is that digit a 1?

steps.instruction: Use the matching symptom tree.
steps.terminal_result: MIL is off with the engine running. If there is a driveability complaint, use the matching engine symptom tree. Historic faults can still be checked on the GCP display faults page (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2).

steps.instruction: Recheck with the GCP display.
steps.terminal_result: Only 1-6-5-4 flashed: no fault codes present (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2). If the MIL stays on while running, check the faults page on the GCP display software and the MIL circuit.

steps.instruction: Follow the manual's procedure for each code.
steps.terminal_result: Look up each DTC in Section 1, Fault Code Description and Index (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.3 onward) for its Section 4 diagnostic page and follow that procedure. Fix codes in the order the manual gives. Faults can only be cleared with the GCP display software (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.2); retest and confirm the MIL stays off.

steps.instruction: Convert the flashed codes first.
steps.terminal_result: This calibration uses the cross-referenced code set: convert each flashed/displayed code with Section 2 (DTC Cross Reference List) first (Ford/EDI GCP Diagnostic Support Manual and DTC Definitions (EDI 1080031), file 'Ford 2_5L Diagnostic Codes.pdf', p.3), then look it up in Section 1 for its Section 4 page and follow that procedure. Clear faults with the GCP display software only (p.2).
